newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds lower with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds lower with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Brady bond prices were lower on Monday amid currency concerns among emerging economies and lack of follow-through buying after last week's tame U.S. inflation data, experts said.

"The market is a bit softer on a combination of the failure of U.S. long bond to do much on what was really dream data and the other is that the currency problems (in Asia and Eastern Europe)" has caused the appetite for risk to decline, said Richard Gray, emerging market analyst at Bank America In London.
News Russia will further delay its announcement on the closing agreement with the London Club of Bank creditors by less than a month also pressured its prices.
Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans were 1/4 lower at 92-1/4 bid and its when-issued IAN bonds were 1/8 softer at 76-1/2 bid.
In the Latin Brady market, experts said investors were likley to focus on Brazil because of concerns over its current account deficit.

Over the weekend, Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said recent currency devalutions in Southeast Asia could undermine investor confidence in emerging economies but confidence in Brazil's economy would be stregnthened by its specific charateristics.

"I think there will be considerable interest in Brazil because of the problems we have seen in the Asian currencies in the last fortnight," said Neil Lockwood, senior economist at ANZ Investment in London.
Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/8 weaker at 83 bid and the country's IDUs were unchanged at 98-3/4 bid.
Elsewhere, market specialists said investors will closely watch the release of the Argentine employment data due to be released on Friday.

"Argentina has their unemployment relase on Friday and there has been quite a lot of unrest about the government's inability to combat unemployment so that will be fairly key especially since the focus is moving toward the elections in October," said Lockwood.
